Aaron Rodgers. An American quarterback widely praised for his exceptional arm talent and clutch performances over a twenty-season career with the Green Bay Packers. Drafted first round, twenty-fourth overall, in 2005, he served as Brett Favre's backup before becoming the starter in 2006. He won the Super Bowl XLV championship during the 2010 season, winning the Super Bowl MVP award. He earned ten Pro Bowl selections from 2011 to 2020 and won one NFL MVP award in 2011. Through his career with Green Bay, he threw for fifty-nine thousand fifty-six passing yards and four hundred seventy-five touchdowns, ranking among the franchise leaders in both. Renowned for his exceptional arm strength and accuracy, he made throws from unconventional angles and delivered balls with precision from anywhere on the field. He's known for his Hail Mary throws and clutch fourth-quarter performances, including several improbable playoff wins and game-winning drives throughout his career. He remained with the Packers through 2021 before finishing with the New York Jets.
